reviews.text:
Nice enough people but very cluttered and unsanitary-looking clinic, and most importantly, pretty dang incompetent doctor. I would go for minor routine procedures, but nothing illness diagnostic or treatment related.

I was grateful they had a same-day opening for me after my cat had puked 10x in 8 hours — typically a sign that something is very wrong, likely an obstruction. I knew that he had a propensity to chew on foreign objects too and told them this. They took an X-Ray which revealed severe constipation but no obstruction, although I knew that not all foreign bodies appear on X-Ray and some require an ultrasound. The doctor insisted that the puking was all due to his stress at home. (Not a stressed cat by any means, btw) He kept asking me if I had left him alone for a while, introduced any random people into the home, etc. I had NOT done any of this in the last 6 months, but I also knew that my cat is very adaptable and has never had an issue with travel, meeting new people, cat-sitters, etc. I just knew that he wasn’t stressed at home, but the doctor insisted that surely SOMETHING must be stressing him out at home. In retrospect, I find it pretty irresponsible for a doctor to say that puking up clear foamy liquid (indication that he hadn’t eaten either) 10x in a night was because of “stress” , especially from a non-stressed cat.

Right before I took my cat home, the female vet tech, I forgot her name but BLESS HER SOUL because she literally saved his life with what she told me: If he pukes again in the next 24h, take him to the ER.

He did puke again and I rushed him to the ER (VEG ER — INCREDIBLE PRACTICE) where he was discovered to have a giant linear obstruction lodged in his stomach but extended all the way down into his intestines, causing plication. DEADLY for a cat.

So yeah. This place is fine for minor procedures like nail clipping, etc. but do not being your cat here if you have any sort of actual health concern.

I have been visiting this clinic for 13 months with my dog and I am always impressed with the attention to detail and teaching of after care for my little dog. Dr. Pruden and her staff make both sick and well visits stress free events.

I love this place!!! Dr. Pruden puts me at ease with my little guy and she asks You questions about how your dog is doing so she can give you the right answers. Just the way she speaks about your pet lets me know she REALLY cares. She’s my vet for life!!! Take your pet there.

Brought our cat in with signs of a possible urinary blockage — straining, no urine, hiding, refusing food and water.
The first thing we walked into was a dog being brought out from treatment without its muzzle on, its owner struggling to get it back on in the middle of the lobby while the dog bit at him. Two other clients were waiting outside on the sidewalk with their cats in carriers because they didn’t feel safe in the room. That should be handled in the exam room by staff, not left to an owner in a full waiting area. I’ve been bitten before and I was on edge from that moment on.
The lobby was dirty, and the exam room was worse: visible trash on the floor and surfaces that had not been cleaned. My partner told me immediately that we should leave.
Then the vet examined him and told us his bladder was “the size of an orange,” that he was blocked, and that this was life-threatening. We said we could take him to BluePearl instead. They advised us to stay and do imaging and blood work here. We agreed — and we ignored everything we had just seen about the condition of this clinic, because we had been told our cat was dying and there was no time.
One hour and twenty minutes later, they came back to tell us their bloodwork equipment was down, so they could not complete the workup, and that they were closing in an hour, so they could not treat him either.
Both of those facts were known before they took him to the back. If you have just told a client their pet is in a life-threatening emergency, and you cannot run labs and you are closing in an hour, you say so at the front desk. It takes ten seconds. Instead we lost two hours and walked out with an X-ray and a bill.
We went to BluePearl. They examined him within 20 minutes, found he was not blocked, and started appropriate treatment.
Two hours of delay on an emergency this clinic diagnosed and then could not act on. If your animal is actually in crisis, go somewhere equipped to handle it.
Every detail above is from that day and I’ll stand behind all of it, including with the invoice and the BluePearl records.
These guys don't honor appointments. Come here if you wanna wait 30+ minutes after making an appointment.

Doctor prudent was AMAZING! So professional and sweet with my dog Luca. They are committed in helping your pets intuitively and not to get a bunch of unnecessary exams and medicines beforehand as other veterinarian clinics. 100% Recommend!

This place will try to up-sell you relentlessly, including outright lies, such as: your dog must have a bordatella vaccine every six months; even if you paid for a wellness exam here 5 months ago, the vet must conduct another one and charge you for it before a rabies vaccine can be administered; only a vet can give a rabies shot, not a tech. These are all absolutely false as I checked them in real time while they were lying to my face. I ended up holding the line on this nonsense but still walked out of there paying $93 for a simple rabies shot, which is outrageous. Not to mention the unclean, extremely cluttered exam "room." Do yourself and your pet a favor and do not go here.

I brought my cat here in the past twice. They overcharge and look for extra stuff to add on bill. If you ever plan on going make sure you are already familiar with your pet and a clinic. Because they absolutely will upsell.It sad that if you really need help,they are more worried about your pockets.  I been stop going here. However I seen other people speaking up so I'm too speaking up.

This was my experience with my companion of 16 years. I brought my 16 year old cat here because she was showing signs of rapid decline and the other vet I had an appointment with couldn't see her sooner.
I expressed on the phone making the appointment that I believe it was the end of life visit as I have had cats my entire life and know the signs. I also expressed my budget and that I'm not someone that can prolong my cats life if they're too far gone.

Immediately out of the carrier before even an general look at her they immediately started cutting her nails! IMMEDIATELY WITHOUT assessing her they went to cut her nails. My cat seized up and collapsed on her side stiff because she was in bad shape and because this is not the way to handle a cat in health distress.
That sent me into tears and I was told that my energy would impact my cat. Of course I'm upset she's dying!

The vet did an ex-ray and said she was in bad shape and she showed me the ex-ray. She said she had so much fluid you couldn't even see the lungs or heart. I asked if there was anything we could do to save her she said it would cost thousands and it would be the same outcome. This to me seemed conclusive.
I had been here before with the prolonging of a cats life for my own selfish reasons and I'm not in the financial situation to do that again.

Upon bringing her to this clinic I knew it would probably be the end of life visit. I did not agree to blood work since the ex ray and doctors words seemed pretty conclusive.
I did not like the way she was handled and I saw terror in her eyes because she was immediately met with clipping her nails at the end of life visit, which to me seemed mean and nasty and unnecessary.

I wrote them expressing my dissatisfaction with her end of life handling getting a response of how they cut nails for safety blah blah blah .It's for their safety because they're afraid or seem to NOT like  or get cats.  She's dying I said she was dying on the phone and she didn't need her nails cut before she dies.  The way they were holding her when giving her the sedative was so strange and she was looking right at me scared for her life. Again i have been through this before and the way the other vet held my other cat was gentle and caring and not like this.

When they responded to my email I get  a response  on how they clip nails always and on how I refused blood work which seemed to be a go to defense response in most of their less than great reviews. I found thiss alarming as I never questioned her diagnosis from the ex-ray. Her diagnosis from the ex ray and the words of the vet was never in questioned by my so why bring that up other than to guilt me or as some defense reflex. Really really  messed up. So this makes me a little suspicious so I ask for a copy of the ex ray, and it's been months and I never have received.

And to top it off they threw away her little bell collar I left there  knowing I was coming back to pick up her ashes (so much for a community vet).

The vet was nice to me she hugged me once my cat had passed  and disarmed me in those moments but also I'm the one paying the  bill and it seems they like humans more than cats.

I feel like the pricing was fair and they were nice enough to me. I feel like the ex ray was conclusive and the vets words were conclusive. but after some time to process my cats final moments which were in terror because she was being handled by people afraid of her or that don't like cats that I had made a terrible call to bring her there.

I had a different experience with my former cat who was 15 and the vet didn't try to trim her nails on her final minutes and she died peacefully in my lap.

This cat deserved that kind of death but instead got one that was hostile.

That's my experience.
Grief is a process it took me two months of processing this experience to write review. Call me psychotic?  Well the way you handled my cat was not with confidence and ease. The tech's body language was fearful and not in control. AND WHO CUTS A DYING CATS NAILS? that is psychotic. She collapsed from it!
